newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB sees at least steady 97 net.
newsitem.headline: ABB sees at least steady 97 net.

text.p: Electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said it expects its 1997 net profit to at least reach 1996's $1.233 billion.
ABB said in a statement released ahead of a news conference that prices for new power plants were not expected to worsen, but rather stabilise at their current low levels.
"Net income for 1997 is expected to reach at least the same level as 1996," ABB said in the statement.
ABB expects the global market for new power plants to expand in emerging markets but remain at a low level in industrial nations.
"Within this competitive environment, 1997 orders and earnings for the power generation segment are expected to reach at least the 1996 level," the ABB statement said.
Orders and earnings in the power transmission and distribution segment are expected to rise due to expansion in emerging markets and productivity increases.
Demand for industrial goods should show good growth in emerging markets, with moderate gains seen in North America.
An improvement in demand in western European markets for standard industrial products and capital goods is not foreseen before early 1998.
Earnings in 1997 at ABB's Industrial and Building Systems segment are expected to remain around the 1996 level as business volumes are flattened by the slowdown in industrial markets.
Earnings and orders for Adtranz should develop positively in 1997 as restructuring effects take hold.
Earnings for the financial services segment are expected to be below the 1996 record performance. -- Peter Nielsen, Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
